attestations.section_title: Introduction to the imparfait
attestations.source_text: The uses of the imparfait (imperfect) are some of the most difficult aspects of French grammar to master. While the passé composé is used to talk about an action that took place on a specific occasion in the past, the imparfait plays a different role. It is used to describe a state of mind and being in the past as well as continuous, repeated, or habitual past actions.

attestations.section_title: Formation of the imparfait
attestations.source_text: To form the imperfect, take the nous form of the present tense and remove the -ons ending, which gives you the stem. Then add the imparfait endings (-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient) to this stem.

attestations.section_title: Formation of the imparfait
attestations.source_text: j’étais, tu étais, il/elle était, nous étions, vous étiez, ils/elles étaient

sections.title: Uses of the imparfait: background and description

attestations.section_title: Uses of the imparfait: background and description
attestations.source_text: Let’s look at the different uses of the imparfait. It is used for background and description. It describes a situation that existed in the past, a state of mind or being. Les rues étaient embouteillées. The streets were jammed. La circulation était fluide. The traffic was flowing. Il faisait trop chaud. It was too hot. Il avait faim. He was hungry. Elle ne savait pas quoi faire. She did not know what to do.

sections.title: The imparfait versus the passé composé

attestations.section_title: The imparfait versus the passé composé
attestations.source_text: As they express a mental or physical state of being, some verbs tend to be used more often in the imparfait than in the passé composé. Among these verbs are: être (to be), avoir (to have), penser (to think), croire (to believe), savoir (to know), espérer (to hope), sembler (to seem), paraître (to appear). However, when these verbs are used in the passé composé, they may take on a different meaning. Il semblait déprimé. He looked depressed. Tout à coup il a semblé comprendre la situation. Suddenly he seemed to understand the situation. Je savais qu’il avait raison. I knew he was right. Immédiatement, j’ai su qu’il était innocent. Immediately, I realized he was innocent.

sections.title: Uses of the imparfait: habitual and repetitive action

attestations.section_title: Uses of the imparfait: habitual and repetitive action
attestations.source_text: Another use of the imparfait is to express habitual, repetitive action. It describes past events that were repeated. Used to and would (meaning habitually) are translated into French by the imparfait. Autrefois, elle faisait partie de la chorale. In the past, she used to belong to the choir. Ils allaient en Inde chaque année. They used to go (would go) to India every year. Il jouait au tennis le mardi. He used to (would) play tennis on Tuesdays.

attestations.section_title: Uses of the imparfait: habitual and repetitive action
attestations.source_text: souvent often fréquemment frequently toujours always le mardi on Tuesdays le vendredi on Fridays chaque jour every day tous les jours every day chaque semaine every week chaque mois every month chaque année every year d’ordinaire ordinarily d’habitude usually habituellement usually régulièrement regularly comme à l’accoutumée as usual autrefois formerly jadis in times past

sections.title: Uses of the imparfait: interrupted continuous action

attestations.section_title: Uses of the imparfait: interrupted continuous action
attestations.source_text: The imparfait is also used to describe a continuous action that was going on in the past when another action (expressed in the passé composé) interrupted it. Elle regardait la télévision quand soudain elle a entendu un grand bruit. She was watching television when suddenly she heard a loud noise. Il faisait ses devoirs quand son frère est arrivé. He was doing his homework when his brother arrived. To express the idea that an action had been going on for a period of time before being interrupted, use the imparfait with depuis. Ils étaient à la montagne depuis une semaine quand ils ont décidé d’aller au bord de la mer. They had been in the mountains for a week when they decided to go to the seashore. Il randonnait depuis trois jours quand il a trouvé cette belle auberge. He had been hiking for three days when he found this beautiful inn.

attestations.section_title: Special construction: si on + imparfait (suggestion)
attestations.source_text: With a si + on construction, the imparfait is used to make a suggestion or to invite someone to do something. The informal on refers to two or more people and is conjugated in the third-person singular. Si on allait en France cet été? What about going to France this summer? Si on achetait des billets? What about buying tickets? Si on allait nager dans le lac? What about going swimming in the lake? Si on allait rendre visite à Léo? What about paying a visit to Léo?

attestations.section_title: Special construction: si seulement + imparfait (wish/regret)
attestations.source_text: You will encounter the imparfait in other idiomatic constructions, for instance, preceded by si seulement, to express a wish or a regret. Si seulement on pouvait prendre des vacances! If only we could take a vacation! Si seulement elle était à l’heure! If only she were on time! Si seulement ils habitaient plus près! If only they lived closer! Si seulement vous saviez! If only you knew!

sections.title: Immediate past in the imparfait (venir de + infinitive)

attestations.section_title: Immediate past in the imparfait (venir de + infinitive)
attestations.source_text: In Chapter 4, you studied the immediate past with the verb venir + de + infinitive. The immediate past can also be used in the imparfait to describe an action that had just happened. Elle vient de téléphoner. She has just called. Elle venait de téléphoner quand il est entré. She had just called when he walked in. Il vient d’accepter ce poste. He just accepted this position. Il venait d’accepter ce poste quand on lui en a proposé un autre. He had just accepted this position when he was offered another one.

grammar_rules.summary: Form the imparfait by taking the nous form of the present tense, removing -ons, and adding the endings -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient.
grammar_rules.explanation: To form the imperfect, take the nous form of the present tense and remove the -ons ending, which gives you the stem. Then add the imparfait endings (-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient) to this stem.
usage: Describe states, habitual actions, continuous actions in the past
common_traps: Do not use the passé composé for habitual actions; use imparfait.

attestations.section_title: Formation of the imparfait
attestations.source_text: To form the imperfect, take the nous form of the present tense and remove the -ons ending, which gives you the stem. Then add the imparfait endings (-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient) to this stem.

grammar_rules.summary: Verbs with spelling changes in the present nous form (e.g., manger, commencer) retain the extra e or ç only for je, tu, il, elle, ils, elles; not for nous, vous.
grammar_rules.explanation: Verbs with spelling changes in the present tense nous form, such as manger and commencer, retain the spelling change only for the je, tu, il, elle, ils, and elles subject pronouns. The extra e or the ç are not needed in the nous and vous forms of the imparfait.
conditions: Applies to verbs like manger, commencer and similar spelling-change verbs
common_traps: Do not add extra e or ç in nous/vous forms.

attestations.source_text: EXERCICE 8·7 Passé composé ou imparfait?

exceptions_and_traps.title: Spelling changes in imparfait
exceptions_and_traps.description: Verbs with spelling changes in the nous present (e.g., manger, commencer) do not take the extra e or ç in the nous and vous forms of the imparfait.

attestations.section_title: Formation of the imparfait
attestations.source_text: The extra e or the ç are not needed in the nous and vous forms of the imparfait.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Irregular stem of être in imparfait
exceptions_and_traps.description: The verb être has an irregular stem ét- in the imparfait, not the expected stem from the nous present.

attestations.section_title: Formation of the imparfait
attestations.source_text: Note that the verb être has an irregular stem in the imparfait.

exceptions_and_traps.title: State verbs: imparfait vs passé composé meaning change
exceptions_and_traps.description: Verbs like être, avoir, penser, croire, savoir, espérer, sembler, paraître tend to be used in imparfait for states; in passé composé they may indicate a specific change or event.
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: Il semblait déprimé (state) vs Tout à coup il a semblé comprendre (change)

attestations.section_title: The imparfait versus the passé composé
attestations.source_text: However, when these verbs are used in the passé composé, they may take on a different meaning.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Distinguishing imparfait and passé composé usage
exceptions_and_traps.description: Use imparfait for description, habitual action, and interrupted continuous action; use passé composé for specific completed events.

attestations.section_title: Introduction to the imparfait
attestations.source_text: While the passé composé is used to talk about an action that took place on a specific occasion in the past, the imparfait plays a different role.
